title: POC onboarding, milestones, benchmarks and exec readout plan - Starlight Systems
summary: Kickoff to align on POC milestones: access/onboarding, bench plan (latency, throughput, cost), midpoint review metrics, and final exec readout. Confirmed sample workload, SSO/KMS requirements, and gating criteria; agreed on 6-week timeline with mid-point demo at week 3.
topics: Benchmark metrics (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens)
Success criteria and exec readout expectations
action_items: Tomasz: open network ticket to grant Redwood IPs access to staging VPC by 2026-05-18
Owen: share benchmark harness and sample prompts (initial) by 2026-05-16
Priya: provide 10 representative prompt templates and token length distribution by 2026-05-15
Maya: send POC statement of work and pricing tiers for Dedicated vs Hosted by 2026-05-17
Amir: send SOC2/ISO questions list and KMS details by 2026-05-19
next_steps: Redwood to provision test model endpoint in sandbox once VPC egress is confirmed
Customer to prioritize prompt set and SLOs for mid-point check
Schedule mid-point review (week 3) and final exec readout (week 6) -- Maya to propose calendar times
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood Solutions), Sara Nguyen (Redwood CSM); Jared Lee (VP Eng), Priya Suresh (ML Eng), Tomasz Kowalski (Infra), Lena Ortiz (Product), Amir Farooqi (Security)

[00:00] Maya Chen: All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call. Uh, Maya here at Redwood, I'll kick things off.
[00:08] Jared Lee: Hey Maya, Jared here.
[00:10] Priya Suresh: Priya.
[00:12] Tomasz Kowalski: Tomasz.
[00:14] Lena Ortiz: Lena.
[00:15] Amir Farooqi: Amir on security.
[00:17] Maya Chen: Great. Owen, do you want to give a 30-second on the bench plan?
[00:21] Owen Patel: Yeah, quick. We'll run two buckets: a latency-focused microbenchmark and a throughput burst test. Latency will capture p50 and p95 on representative prompts at the customer sequence length distribution, tokens per request. Throughput is tokens-per-second and RPS under steady-state. We'll measure cost per 1M tokens for both Hosted and a Dedicated baseline with our typical quantization profile.
[00:40] Priya Suresh: When you say "representative prompts" — we'll provide templates, but token distribution matters; we have short queries and longer context expansions.
[00:48] Owen Patel: Totally. Please send the token histogram — that's actually the main input for kernel selection and batching config.
[00:53] Priya Suresh: Ok we'll export that from our inference logs.
[00:56] Maya Chen: High level agenda for today: align milestones (kickoff access, mid-point review, final exec readout), confirm success criteria, list access needs (VPC peering or egress, SSO, KMS), and agree next steps.
[01:08] Jared Lee: Our exec care about latency p95 under 250ms for the primary production path and cost under X amount — we'll put numbers in the doc.
[01:16] Maya Chen: Helpful to have hard numbers; we usually recommend p95 < 200ms to be conservative but we'll target whatever you set.
[01:22] Lena Ortiz: Also want a clear ROI narrative for the readout: reduction in API latency for customers and cost delta vs current self-hosting.
[01:29] Diego Ramos: We can produce a delta slide that shows cost per 1M tokens hosted vs your current infra, and expected ops savings.
[01:36] Amir Farooqi: Quick security note: we need to know where keys live — KMS/HSM, whether Redwood stores anything, and audit logs retention.
[01:44] Sara Nguyen: We'll share our security one-pager. We support customer-managed KMS for Private; for Hosted there are options. We'll clarify in the SOW.
[01:52] Tomasz Kowalski: For network, we prefer egress from our staging VPC to be restricted; is there a static Redwood egress IP range you can provide?
[02:00] Maya Chen: Yes, we can provide a list of IPs for the sandbox endpoints. We'll put that in the action items.
[02:06] Priya Suresh: Regarding benchmarks — are you going to run with our model or Redwood's served model variants? We plan to ship our fine-tuned LlamaX v2 variant.
[02:15] Owen Patel: We can do both. For performance parity we run your fine-tuned model if you can provide the weights and a deployment path (we support common containerization formats and model repos). Alternatively we can run comparable open models from our catalog to characterize runtime behavior.
[02:29] Priya Suresh: We'll need to check licensing for shipping weights, but we can start with a functional equivalence test using an open model.
[02:36] Jared Lee: Timeline expectation — can we do a 6-week POC? Kickoff this week, mid-point at week 3, and exec readout at week 6.
[02:44] Maya Chen: That's our typical cadence. Week 1: access & onboarding; week 2: baseline bench run; week 3: mid-point demo and plan pivot; weeks 4–5: optimizations and scale tests; week 6: exec readout and SOW/contract discussion if green.
[02:58] Lena Ortiz: For the mid-point, what should we be prepared with? Screens, sample prompts, and success/failure log?
[03:04] Owen Patel: Exactly — we'll run an initial benchmark and produce a slide deck with p50/p95, tokens per second, costs, and example outputs. We also include regression checks against your eval prompts.
[03:14] Tomasz Kowalski: On the VPC front — we prefer to run tests against a staging cluster behind our NAT. We'll need Redwood to have a test endpoint accessible over TLS from staging.
[03:23] Maya Chen: OK, we'll need the network ticket from you to open egress and the security contact.
[03:27] Amir Farooqi: I'll own that. We also need an NDA addendum for telemetry.
[03:31] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll send standard telem NDA language.
[03:34] Priya Suresh: For success criteria, I'm thinking: 1) p95 latency <= 250ms for 90% of test cases; 2) throughput scale to 4x current baseline without p95 degradation; 3) cost per 1M tokens less than our projected threshold after quantization. Doable?
[03:47] Owen Patel: Those are good. For the 4x throughput, we should define the baseline RPS or tokens/sec. If you share the baseline we'll dimension Dedicated vs Hosted.
[03:56] Jared Lee: Baseline is ~450 tokens/sec sustained across our steady traffic pattern.
[04:02] Owen Patel: Great. We'll design the bench to ramp to 1800 tokens/sec and capture tails.
[04:06] Diego Ramos: Also propose adding a cold-start KV-cache hit-rate metric; long context runs can have cache misses that impact latency.
[04:14] Priya Suresh: Good call. We'll include long-context transcripts.
[04:18] Maya Chen: Let's walk through the access checklist: SSO (SAML) for Redwood Console? or do you want service accounts?
[04:25] Tomasz Kowalski: Service accounts for infra access, SAML for dashboard users.
[04:29] Maya Chen: Noted. KMS — do you want customer-managed keys for the Private deployment?
[04:35] Amir Farooqi: Ideally yes. For Hosted we need to understand what subset of data leaves the VPC and how logs are stored.
[04:41] Sara Nguyen: We'll document log retention policies and options for audit logs export.
[04:45] Lena Ortiz: On artifacts for the exec readout, we want a short narrative plus 3 slides: executive summary, cost/latency delta, and recommended next steps.
[04:54] Maya Chen: We'll prepare that readout template and share it ahead of the final meeting.
[04:58] Owen Patel: Quick technical constraint — if you use extremely long sequences more than 8k tokens, some quantization modes change perf characteristics; please flag any outliers.
[05:07] Priya Suresh: We have < 4k 95th percentile for context, so should be workable.
[05:11] Maya Chen: Great. Now let's enumerate gating criteria for POC success — propose: latency gate, throughput gate, functional parity gate, and security/compliance gate.
[05:21] Jared Lee: Agree. For functional parity, we want a CLI of model quality: no more than 5% drop in BLEU/ROUGE on our eval set or equivalent human-sign-off.
[05:30] Owen Patel: We'll run both automated metrics and sample human review. We'll capture any regression with examples and mitigate via prompt engineering or model variant selection.
[05:39] Priya Suresh: If you see hallucination spikes, we need RMS logging — who will own triage?
[05:45] Diego Ramos: Our SEs will pair with your ML engineers to triage, and we'll log anomalous outputs with trace IDs.
[05:52] Jas: [inaudible] 
[05:54] Maya Chen: (laughs) we lost someone — ok moving on.
[05:58] Lena Ortiz: Any cost model suggestion — how do you estimate cost for the readout slide?
[06:03] Diego Ramos: We'll present two numbers: a unit cost (per 1M tokens) and an operational estimate (including reserved Dedicated amortized). We'll show hosted per-token bill and dedicated amortized capex/ops.
[06:14] Priya Suresh: For Dedicated, we need guaranteed throughput. What are your SLOs?
[06:19] Maya Chen: For Dedicated we offer committed throughput and SLA-backed latency targets—details are in the dedicated contract template; we can share a draft.
[06:27] Amir Farooqi: Also include rollback/fallback policies. If Dedicated nodes are saturated, what's the graceful degradation path?
[06:33] Owen Patel: We support automatic fallback to smaller model variants or cross-region fallback to avoid hard errors; we'll demo that in week 4 if needed.
[06:41] Priya Suresh: For benchmarks, what harness do you use? JMeter-style or custom runner?
[06:47] Owen Patel: We use a custom harness that supports token-level pacing, KV cache priming, and trace IDs. We'll share a reproducible harness (Docker image + scripts).
[06:56] Maya Chen: Okay next — schedule items. We'll plan for a check-in next Monday to confirm access tickets. Mid-point review third Friday from now. Maya will send invites.
[07:06] Jared Lee: Works. Also, can you provide a sample runbook for on-call handling during the tests? Tomasz will need that.
[07:13] Diego Ramos: Yes, we'll provide an ops runbook with playbook steps for common failures and contact rotations.
[07:19] Priya Suresh: One more question: if we need private deployment in our on-prem later, how does data residency work during the POC?
[07:27] Sara Nguyen: For POC we can run in your staging VPC with customer-managed KMS; for on-prem we have an option but that would be a separate engagement.
[07:36] Amir Farooqi: We need to run a short security checklist before any weights are transferred.
[07:40] Maya Chen: We'll include that as an action item — Amir will send the checklist.
[07:44] Priya Suresh: Do you recommend any quantization profile prior to benching? 4-bit or 8-bit?
[07:50] Owen Patel: Start with 8-bit for parity and then test 4-bit int8-like variants for cost delta; some models will show quality regressions at 4-bit. We'll show both.
[07:59] Jared Lee: On dataset sharing, we'll scrub PII but keep representative context.
[08:03] Maya Chen: Perfect. Alright let's recap concrete owners — Tomasz will open the network ticket, Priya will send the prompt set and token histogram, Amir will send security checklist and KMS details, Owen will share the harness and initial bench config, Maya will send SOW and readout template.
[08:20] Lena Ortiz: And timeline: access by week 1, baseline bench end of week 2, mid-point review week 3, optimizations through week 5, final readout week 6.
[08:32] Maya Chen: Any blockers?
[08:34] Tomasz Kowalski: Just the network ticket and licensing for weights.
[08:37] Priya Suresh: We'll confirm weights licensing by end of week.
[08:40] Maya Chen: Great. We'll follow up with the calendar invites and action-item email. Thanks everyone.
[08:45] Jared Lee: Thanks.
[08:46] Priya Suresh: Thanks.
[08:47] Tomasz Kowalski: Thanks.

Post-meeting notes:
- Mid-point metrics: plan to present p50/p95, tokens/sec, KV cache hit-rate, cost-per-1M-tokens; include a small slide on fallback behavior.
- Exec readout deliverables: 5–8 slide deck + appendix with raw bench results and SOW draft.
- Risk items: weight transfer/legal, VPC egress configuration, potential quality regressions on low-bit quantization.

References / shared artifacts mentioned:
- Redwood benchmark harness (link to be provided by Owen)
- Security one-pager (to be sent by Sara)
- Draft SOW and pricing (to be sent by Maya)

End of transcript.
